resolvedDefects.F-1: RFC 3164 line without HOSTNAME lost its first key=value field into the header in both executors. Resolved by BSD_HOSTNAME and the rfc3164_hostless rule of contracts/syslog-header-grammar.v1.json.
resolvedDefects.F-2: RFC 5424 VERSION policy differed between consumers. Resolved by semantics.rfc5424SupportedVersions, read by every consumer.
resolvedDefects.F-3: U+2028 inside a value was rejected by the browser and parsed by the generated Ruby. Resolved by the portable token REST = [^\r\n]+.
resolvedDefects.F-4: RFC 5424 TIMESTAMP with an impossible calendar day was rejected by the browser and parsed by the generated Ruby. Resolved by an explicit calendar check beside Time.iso8601 in both Ruby templates.
resolvedDefects.F-5: A TAG directly after the timestamp ('kernel:', 'sshd[123]:') was read as HOSTNAME by both executors when HOSTNAME was omitted. Resolved by BSD_HOSTNAME not ending in ':'; the line is declined.
resolvedDefects.F-6: The Python Multi-Pass fallback parsed an RFC 5424 line with VERSION 999. Resolved by semantics.rfc5424SupportedVersions and the rfc5424_version_head fragment, read by every Python entry point.
resolvedDefects.F-7: The strict key=value path of the browser and the generated Ruby accepted U+001C..U+001F as value data while Generic Structural and the Python preview declined the line (issue #214). Resolved by KV_BARE excluding U+001C..U+001F.
resolvedDefects.F-8: The Python Multi-Pass key=value scanner split pairs at Unicode white space (NBSP, U+2028) and decoded a different escape set than the browser and Ruby. Resolved by the scanner reading fragments.kv_pair and semantics.kvUnescapedAfterBackslash.
resolvedDefects.F-9: A CEF or LEEF line with U+2028 inside a value was rejected by the browser ('.' excludes it in ECMAScript) and parsed by the generated Ruby and the Python preview. Resolved by dotAll on the two family head expressions.
resolvedDefects.F-10: The Python preview reported a line that claims to be CEF or LEEF but is not valid (six header fields, LEEF 3.0) as parsed through its permissive Generic Structural fallback, with multi-word values cut at the first space. Resolved for the Python preview by fragments.structured_family_claim. The browser and Ruby side is owner policy D-2.
resolvedDefects.F-11: CEF and LEEF: the header splitter also decoded backslash escapes in the extension, which the extension grammar then decoded a second time, identically in the browser and the generated Ruby. 'filePath=C:\\\\Users\\\\new' came out as 'C:\\Users' LF 'ew', and the standard's own example 'act=blocked a \\\\ dst=1.1.1.1' lost dst. Resolved by keeping the text after the last header delimiter exactly as written.
resolvedDefects.F-12: The Python preview offered a comma row with a double quote inside a bare field (aaa,b\"bb,ccc) as a CSV candidate; RFC 4180 forbids it and the browser tokenizer and Ruby's CSV.parse_line reject the row. Resolved in parse_csv_spans.
resolvedDefects.F-13: The Python preview parsed a CEF:1 line while the browser and the generated Ruby implement CEF version 0 only, so the Analyze step showed a line as parsed that the generated parser rejects. Resolved by semantics.cefSupportedVersions, read by every engine.

A backslash followed by another character is header text as written. Found on 2026-11-15 by the three-way comparison with the Python preview.

Product policy in the grammar contract (semantics.cefSupportedVersions = ["0"]): the generated parser implements CEF version 0 only, so a CEF:1 line is declined by every engine instead of being shown as parsed by the preview and then rejected by the artifact

csvCases.provenance: RFC 4180 section 2: rule 4, fields are separated by commas
RFC 4180 section 2: rule 5, each field may be enclosed in double quotes
RFC 4180 section 2: rule 6, a field containing a comma is enclosed in double quotes
RFC 4180 section 2: rule 7, a double quote inside an enclosed field is escaped by a preceding double quote
RFC 4180 section 2: rule 5, double quotes may not appear inside a field that is not enclosed

Found on 2026-11-15 by the format-level browser/Ruby fuzz that followed the independent re-audit. RFC 4180 section 2: rules 5 to 7: a field is enclosed in one pair of double quotes, and a double quote inside it is written twice. In ""aaa"" the field closes after its second character and text follows the closing quote. CSV.parse_line of Ruby 2.4.9 counts quotation marks and returned the field "aaa" with quotation marks.

Found on 2026-11-15 by the format-level browser/Ruby fuzz that followed the independent re-audit. Product rule for the CSV format: SP and TAB at the edge of an unquoted field are stripped, nothing else is (the generated parser on Ruby 2.4.9). A form feed is field data; the browser removed it.

Found on 2026-11-15 by the format-level browser/Ruby fuzz that followed the independent re-audit. A row that holds nothing but spaces is not an event: the generated parser reports that no CSV event was parsed. The browser returned one empty field as a complete parse of a one-column layout.

jsonCases.provenance: RFC 8259: section 13 example (one object of the array): numbers and strings as members of an object
RFC 8259: section 7: \uXXXX (with a surrogate pair for U+1F600), \/, \\, \" and \n name single characters
RFC 8259: section 7: only quotation mark, reverse solidus and U+0000..U+001F must be escaped; U+2028 may appear as itself
RFC 8259: section 4: members are separated by commas; a comma is not followed by the closing brace

Product policy on RFC 8259 section 4 (names SHOULD be unique; behaviour for repeated names is unpredictable): an object with a repeated name is declined by every engine rather than keeping one of the values

Found by the independent re-audit of 2026-11-15. RFC 8259: section 7: the escapes are \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t and \uXXXX; \x41 is not one of them. The json library of Ruby 2.4.9 dropped the backslash and returned 10.5.5.x416.
Found by the independent re-audit of 2026-11-15. RFC 8259: section 2: the grammar has no comments. The json library of Ruby 2.4.9 skips /* */ and // comments.

Found by the independent re-audit of 2026-11-15. RFC 8259: section 7 and 8.2: a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane is a high surrogate followed by a low surrogate; two high surrogates name no character. The json library of Ruby 2.4.9 joined them into U+1F43D.
RFC 8259: section 8.2 and RFC 3629 section 3: an unpaired surrogate is not a character and has no UTF-8 encoding, so the event cannot be sent on unchanged.

Found on 2026-11-15 by the format-level browser/Ruby fuzz that followed the independent re-audit. Parsing Success Contract: an event from which no field was extracted is not a parsed event. The generated Ruby emitted an event without fields for an empty object; the browser reported UNKNOWN.

RFC 8259 section 6: implementations that use IEEE 754 binary64 are interoperable only for numbers within its precision. A decimal with more than 15 significant digits is not the value a double holds; reporting the rounded double as the value of the event would be reporting a number the event does not contain, so no engine may report the event as parsed (src/jsonNumberSafety.ts). Found on 2026-11-15 by the three-way comparison: the Python preview reported the rounded value.

RFC 8259 section 6: integers outside [-(2^53)+1, (2^53)-1] are not interoperable. 1e16 names such an integer in exponent spelling; the browser and the generated Ruby decline the event, and so must the Python preview (which keeps only an integer written as an integer exactly). Found on 2026-11-15 by the three-way comparison.

RFC 8259 section 6: a number outside the range of binary64 is not interoperable. 1e-400 is not zero, and a double holds zero for it; no engine may report the event as parsed with p = 0 (src/jsonNumberSafety.ts).

RFC 8259 section 9: an implementation may set limits on the maximum depth of nesting. The JSON source contract of the product is eight nested levels (src/jsonSourceSafety.ts, enforced by the browser and by the generated Ruby); a value at the ninth level declines the event in every engine. Found on 2026-11-15 by the three-way comparison: the Python preview read forty levels.
